Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Dilip Kumar, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Rajrshi Gupta, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha, learned AGA for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 636 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Gurshaiganj, District Kannauj during pendency of the trial.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that this is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant.

The first bail application of the applicant was dismissed by this Court vide order dated 08.05.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 19092 of 2023.
5.

6. He further submits that even post mortem report suggests that deceased died due to hanging.

He further submits that applicant is in jail since 01.12.2022 i.e. for last more than a year and till date only three prosecution witness could be examined out of total 14 prosecution witness, therefore,
there is no hope of early disposal of the trial.
He further submits that considering the facts and circumstances of the case, applicant should be enlarged on bail.

7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that this is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant and applicant is husband of the deceased but he could not dispute the fact that applicant has taken a specific plea that as one of the child of the deceased was disabled, therefore, she committed suicide and his defence finds support from the statements of the parents of deceased recorded before the trial court.
He further could not dispute the fact that applicant is in jail since 01.12.2022 i.e. for last more than a year and according to the post mortem report deceased died due to hanging.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
9. This is second bail application filed on behalf of the applicant.

The first bail application of the applicant was dismissed by this Court on merit and from perusal of the order dated 08.05.2023 passed by this Court, it appears that the first bail application of the applicant was dismissed on the ground that however applicant has taken a defence that one child of the deceased was disabled since birth, therefore, under depression she committed suicide but with regard to disability of the child no material could be brought on record by the applicant but in the instant second bail application applicant by way of supplementary affidavit annexed the statements of parents and brother of the deceased, which were recorded by the trial court and from perusal of the same, it appears that they accepted this fact that one child of the deceased was disabled since birth.
10.

Further, however, applicant is husband but he is in jail since December, 2022 i.e. for last more than a year and till date out of 14 prosecution witnesses only three prosecution witness could be examined, therefore, there is no hope of early disposal of the trial.

11. Further, post mortem report of the deceased suggests that she died due to hanging, therefore,
defence taken by the applicant that due to disability of the son, deceased committed suicide cannot be completely brushed aside.

12. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
13. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

sentences.text: Let the applicant - Rishabh @ Golu be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
15. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

16. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
